title: Unbounded Result Set Queries (Out-of-Memory Risk)
damaged_code:
```sql
SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE user_id = 123; -- Returns millions of rows
```
pattern: Executing database queries that fetch matching rows without an explicit cap or range constraint (`LIMIT`, `TOP`, or `rownum`).
why_bad: If the tables grow over time, unconstrained select queries bring massive volumes of data into application memory at once, risking heap exhaustion, severe garbage collection thrashing, and database locks.
detection: SQL select queries or ORM finders (`findAll()`, `all()`) executed in user-facing APIs without paging, slicing, or row caps.
counterexample: Static, small reference tables (e.g., country codes or state lists). `Context-dependent`.
fix: Always enforce explicit query bounds using `LIMIT`, pagination controls, or database-side cursors.
